author: @FrankCurzio
text:
Gold's pain finally has an end date.

It has now fallen as much as 3% to around $3,735, its lowest since September 2025. That's well below the $3,790 from my last post.

And the dollar briefly hit a fresh 19-month high. Traders see a 95% chance of a December rate hike.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem laid out the math. He wants interest rates, after inflation, at 2% to 2.5% by spring. He thinks they're a full point short. That's a hike in December, January, March AND April.

Every hike makes holding gold a worse deal. A stronger dollar knocks it down a second time.

Back in October I said we'd see at least four more hikes. Now a Fed president is saying up to four... with dates on them.

Cheap gold won't turn this around by itself. The turn comes when the Fed is done, and that clock now points to spring.

So I'm in no rush to buy gold at full size before then.

-

For anyone new here, I'm Frank. 30 years on Wall Street, and I post what's moving the market as it happens. Follow me @FrankCurzio for more.

author: @rubicon59
text: A bombshell after bombshell, delivered matter-of-factly.  $SPCX $TSLA
quoted_text:
Elon Musk at TomorrowX (my notes, left slightly early)

Grok 4.8:

- In the RL phase now. The goal is to make it as useful as possible, not to max out benchmarks. He called benchmark chasing a "fool's errand."

- Same playbook as FSD: trace every failure back to bad, biased, or missing data, fix the data, retrain.

- Versions get soft-launched under Grok Bot. Whether users actually got their problem solved feeds back into training as a data flywheel.

- Usefulness test, Carmack-style. Open a toy RC car box, put the batteries in, screw the lid back on, drive it.

Optimus:

- Household chores like trash and dishes (wash, dry, put away) in 12 to 18 months.

- First real use case is heavy industry running 24/7, 168 hrs a week. Think mining and refining ore for US national security.

- Later in the home: tutor, babysitter, mowing, cooking dinner.

Cybercab / Robotaxi:

- Rolling out slowly on purpose. No steering wheel and no pedals means one bad accident could shut the program down.

- No serious injuries or accidents so far. In Austin you can get one within minutes.

- Next up: other big Texas cities. California approval hoped for maybe early next year.

Terafab:

- The plan is a 100M sq ft footprint, the biggest build on Earth.

- Starts with standard tools, pushes suppliers for custom machine versions, and may build its own machines.

- R&D fab with first test chip around June next year (8 to 9 months out). Phase 1 volume production toward end of 2028.

- The bet: legacy fabs are CapEx-averse, so taking more risk and moving faster should get to a more efficient process. Elon is "cautiously optimistic."

xAI compute:

- Data centers are built by an in-house crew ("Army X") plus contractors. Every task is broken down so it can be trained in a few days.

- Tesla Megapacks smooth out GPU power swings. Without them, training runs get messy and turbine shafts can literally break.

- Adding about 0.5 GW a month right now, which is roughly 220k GB300s plus networking and cooling. Target is over 1 GW a month by end of next year.
Orbital compute (Starline)

- Aiming for 200 GW a year of solar panel manufacturing for space. That's about 40% of average US power usage. Starship supplies the launch tonnage.

-He called the Starline AI satellite simpler than Starlink V3, and SpaceX already has 11k+ satellites in orbit.

-Solar produces about 250 W/m². The double-sided radiator dumps about 1,200 W/m². So roughly 5:1 panel area to radiator area.

- The compute core is about 1/4 the size of a VR NVL72 rack with the same capability, laser-linked to Starlink.

Neuralink:

- Several hundred employees. 30+ people have the implant.

- The first product (I think it's Telepathy) lets tetraplegics control phones, computers, or a robot arm just by thinking, including feeding themselves.

- Longer term, he's confident they can route brain signals around spinal damage so people can walk again.
The thread connecting all of it: power, chips, and data are being pulled in-house across every company.
